title: Queen's Gambit Accepted (2...dxc4)
intro: Black takes on c4 and gives up the centre. Seize the middle with 3.e4, push e5 against ...Nf6, and break up ...b5 with a4.

lessons.title: Seizing the centre with 3.e4
lessons.summary: Claim the centre with e4 and meet ...e5 with Nf3.

steps.text: In the Queen's Gambit Accepted, Black takes on c4 and leaves the centre wide open.
Claim the full centre and open the way for your bishop to win c4 back.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.e4: you take the centre while threatening Bxc4.
steps.ifRight: White controls e4 and d4 side by side.

steps.text: Black attacks your centre at once with 3...e5.
Develop and defend d4 while attacking e5.
steps.hint: Put your king's knight on f3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Nf3: dxe5 lets Black trade queens with ...Qxd1+.
steps.ifRight: You keep the queens on and build pressure against e5.

steps.text: Win back the c4 pawn with tempo.
steps.hint: Capture on c4 with your bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Bxc4: your pieces develop quickly and target f7.
steps.ifRight: Next White castles and plays Nxd4 or Qb3.

steps.text: Here Black played 3...Nf6 to attack e4. Gain space with tempo.
steps.hint: Push the e-pawn forward to attack the knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.e5: after 4...Nd5 5.Bxc4, White keeps a strong centre and active pieces.
steps.ifRight: Black's knight must move again while White wins back c4.

steps.text: Club players often try to hold onto the extra c4 pawn with 3...b5.
Undermine the b5 pawn right away.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.a4: Black cannot keep both pawns together.
steps.ifRight: If Black tries ...c6, axb5 breaks the chain open.

steps.text: Black tries to hold b5 with 4...c6.

steps.ifWrong: Play 5.axb5: after 5...cxb5, the rook on a8 is exposed and Nc3 hits b5.
steps.ifRight: Notice the rook on a8 behind the b5 pawn.

steps.text: Attack b5 and target the a8 rook.
steps.hint: Develop the queen's knight to c3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nc3: White wins back material with a big lead in development.
steps.ifRight: If Black defends b5 with ...a6, Nxb5 wins anyway because ...axb5 loses the a8 rook.

lessons.title: Meeting 3...c5 and 3...Nc6
lessons.summary: Push d5 against ...c5 and develop smoothly against ...Nc6.

steps.text: Black may also strike at d4 from the flank with 3...c5.
Push past to gain central space and keep c4 cut off.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.d5: your central pawns cramp Black and c4 will fall soon.
steps.ifRight: White enjoys a huge space advantage.

steps.text: Defend e4 and develop a piece.
steps.hint: Bring the b1 knight to c3.
steps.ifRight: White will win c4 with Bxc4 and develop smoothly.

steps.text: If Black attacks d4 with 3...Nc6, develop and protect d4.
steps.hint: Bring out the king's knight or push d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Nf3 (or 4.Be3): d4 is protected and White prepares Bxc4.
steps.ifRight: White keeps a commanding centre and wins c4 back effortlessly.

steps.text: Against 3...e6, win back the pawn right away.
steps.hint: Capture on c4 with your bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Bxc4 to recover the pawn and take a big lead in development.
steps.ifRight: White has a dream centre and rapid development.
